subject: QBR prep: infra econ playtest & capacity knobs
messages:

Date: 2026-09-07T09:12:00Z
Subject: QBR prep: infra econ playtest & capacity knobs

Team — kicking off a short thread to stitch together the infra numbers we need for the QBR (next Tuesday). Goal: give execs a tight, reproducible narrative on how three levers move our unit economics and risk profile over the next 90 days: 1) GPU commit/turn-downs, 2) batching + dynamic batching policies, 3) prefix/KV caching hit rates.

Quick asks (can each person reply inline):
- Vivek: can you attach the latest capacity model (per-region GPU hours, committed vs burst, blended cost) and a short sensitivity table showing spend @ 65/75/85% util?
- Lauren: can you call out any OKR asks we should surface (capacity safety buffer, canary traffic % for new quantization)?
- Laura: can you flag any external procurement / contract constraints that would change if we recommend moving 10–20% traffic to Dedicated or private nodes?

I attached a draft capacity_model_v2.xlsx and a quick sim of batching_cache_simulations.csv — both rough but enough to iterate. I'll consolidate into a one-pager for the QBR slides once we have numbers.

Diego
Staff Product Manager, Infra Economics
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: QBR prep: infra econ playtest & capacity knobs

Thanks Diego — good framing. Two quick bullets from me:

- OKRs: we should propose a conservative safety buffer band (5% committed buffer, 10% burst headroom) and a separate rapid rollback path for any quantization rollout (canary at 1% + 5% after 24h if error rates stable). Call this out as an operations ask rather than a permanent capacity ask.
- Slides: keep the exec page to a single chart (spend vs latency tradeoff) and a short risks column (networking constraints, procurement lead time).

I'll surface the OKR language in my next note and I agree with the three levers.

Lauren
VP, Platform

Date: 2026-09-08T08:05:00Z
Subject: Re: QBR prep: infra econ playtest & capacity knobs

Adding the capacity numbers and a short readout — attaching updated capacity_model_v2.xlsx and batching_cache_simulations.csv with a new tab called "sensitivity_summary." Highlights:

- Blended GPU cost (monthly): $2.1M at current commit.
- Utilization scenarios: 65% util -> $2.8M spend (inefficient), 75% util -> $2.1M, 85% util -> $1.7M (improved unit economics).
- Batching + dynamic batching impact: avg tokens/sec per-GPU improves 18–38% depending on request size mix; that reduces per-token cost by ~12% at conservative assumptions.
- KV/prefix cache: raising hit rate from 40% -> 60% reduces tail token generation work and cuts effective cost by another ~6% in our model (sensitive to prompt reuse distribution).
- Risk: moving 10–20% traffic to Dedicated reduces marginal latency variance but increases committed cost by ~$220k/mo unless we reclaim idle units.

Attachments included: capacity_model_v2.xlsx (with sensitivity_summary tab), batching_cache_simulations.csv (per-workload sims), qbr_onepager_v1.pdf (one-slide summary).

I'll also include a small Monte Carlo sheet that shows probability of exceeding committed capacity given the Q4 forecast (sharing if helpful).

Vivek
Director, Infrastructure Economics

Forwarding to ACME operations to validate procurement/contract implications. Sarah — quick context: we are evaluating a recommendation to shift 10–20% of traffic into a Dedicated pool (either Redwood Dedicated or ACME private nodes depending on compliance). Vivek attached the sensitivity table — key question for procurement: if we recommend a 6–12 month committed increase, what are the minimum notice periods and any early-termination or scaling clauses that would materially change the cost calculus?

Can you confirm: 1) minimum lead time for 20% additional GPUs in us-west, 2) any temporary spot-to-dedicated trade programs, 3) whether there are region-specific constraints (power, quotas) that would change the latency story?

Laura
Head of Sales Ops, Redwood Inference

Thanks everyone — brief consolidation below (final asks so I can lock the one-pager and slides):

Action items (owners & targets):
- Vivek: finalize the sensitivity tables and add the Monte Carlo sheet (+ add a row for cost w/ 15% traffic on Dedicated) — due 2026-09-10 10:00 PT.
- Lauren: write the OKR ask language (safety buffer + canary rollout path) and the single-slide narrative — due 2026-09-10 12:00 PT.
- Laura / ACME: confirm procurement constraints and lead times (reply to thread) — requested by 2026-09-10 18:00 PT.
- Diego: consolidate slide and send to execs by end of day 2026-09-10.

Exec slide preview (single-paragraph):
We recommend a targeted 10–15% Dedicated traffic pilot to reduce latency variance for high-value customers while retaining 5% committed buffer and 10% burst headroom. At conservative utilization assumptions (75% baseline) this yields an expected monthly spend delta of ~$120–220k; combined batching and cache improvements can offset ~15–18% of the incremental spend while improving per-token latency. Risks: procurement lead time and the operational complexity of pinned capacity.

Please reply only to confirm or to raise material blockers — I'll assume silence means agreement and will produce the final PDF.

Diego
Staff Product Manager, Infra Economics
Redwood Inference
